# Aion Write-Amplification Forensics — 2026-08-17

READ-ONLY investigation. Nothing written to the store, no locks taken; all store access was direct file reads of immutable content-addressed blobs plus the live server's own read paths (`aion list`, `aion describe`). Companion doc: `aion-store-census-20260817.md` (totals, shard table, age curve — settled there, not re-derived here). This doc answers the question that census left open: **what mechanism turns kilobytes of honest content into ~432 MB/run of permanent store?**

Store: `/Users/tom/Developer/ablative/stack/aion/aion-data` — 107.94 GB apparent bytes, 286,847 node files at measurement time, 238 runs ⇒ **453 MB/run average** (census's 432 MB, plus a day's growth). Node files are zstd blobs, immutable, mtime = creation time, so an mtime-window census measures exactly the bytes a run wrote — and, because nothing ever deletes them (see §4), exactly the bytes it permanently keeps.

## 1. The three subject runs — stored vs honest

| Run | Type / status | Window (UTC) | Store bytes written (files) | Honest transcript payload | History (D-keyspace) | Multiplier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `4da9963a-4f3d-4287-9ea4-d4d0fd8336ce` | git_status_sweep, Completed | Aug-17 08:10:21–08:10:46 (25 s) | **73.7 MB** (705 files; 676 in shard-21) | **136,442 B** (338 `Message` events, ~404 B each — status lines) | 33,110 B (12 events) | **~540×** |
| `0dad5237-72a7-49e3-838c-111a5a54c377` | norn_dev, Completed | Aug-16 15:43:37–16:00:04 (16.5 m) | **2.98 GB** (2,444 files; shards 44+32) | **26,638,342 B** (1,714 events) | 51,442 B (14 events) | **~112×** |
| `4c4ef686-ccc7-49d7-a352-63df61f6f3da` | norn_dev, Failed | Aug-16 02:20:16–04:40:09 (2 h 20 m) | **6.96 GB** (9,387 files; shard-56 ≈ 5.0 GB, shard-51 ≈ 1.94 GB) | **~66.9 MB** (19.5 MB + 47.4 MB across its two stream leaves) | 39,081 B (16 events) | **~104×** |

Sweep ticks generally: 29 consecutive sweeps Aug-16 22:00 → Aug-17 08:39 wrote **5.91 GB total, avg 204 MB/tick, max 663 MB** (`91af66c8`, 49 s) — Tom's "hundreds of MB per status sweep" is measured fact. The tick cost varies with how fat the leaf its events land in happens to be (§3).

The `describe` history (the workflow's actual durable oplog — the decisions) is **33–51 KB per run**. All volume lives in the `O`-keyspace activity-transcript streams and, overwhelmingly, in superseded storage-tree nodes.

### Per-event-type tables (transcript payloads, subject run only)

**Failed norn_dev `4c4ef686`, shard-51 stream (2,921 events, 47,384,015 B):**

| kind | n | bytes |
|---|---|---|
| Raw/response.in_progress | 178 | 14,577,193 |
| Raw/response.created | 178 | 14,576,480 |

| Raw/response_item | 339 | 587,674 |
| Raw/response.output_item.done | 345 | 578,600 |

**Completed norn_dev `0dad5237` (1,714 events, 26,638,342 B):** Raw/response.completed 92×8,234,156 B · Raw/response.in_progress 92×8,217,252 B · Raw/response.created 92×8,216,884 B · everything else <1.9 MB.

**Sweep `4da9963a` (338 events, 136,442 B):** 100% `Message`, ~404 B each.

Note the honest-content layer has its own duplication: `response.created` / `response.in_progress` / `response.completed` are each a **full provider response envelope (~82 KB avg) carrying the entire instructions block**, persisted three times per LLM turn — ~91% of transcript bytes. But even taking that 67 MB as "honest", the store cost is 100–540× on top of it. The structural amplifier is below.

## 2. The mechanism — whole-leaf re-persistence per event append

The named write path, file:line:

1. **One event = one append = one tree commit.** The server publishes every agent telemetry event individually: `crates/aion-server/src/activity_publisher.rs:183` → `self.store.append_activity_event(expected_seq, &event)`; `crates/aion-store-haematite/src/store.rs:1617` → `store.append_batch(&stream_key, &[payload.as_slice()], expected_seq)` — a batch of ONE. No coalescing (confirmed empirically: sweep wrote 676 shard-21 files for 338 events — one new leaf + one new root per event).
2. **Each commit rewrites the entire containing leaf.** Haematite's mutation path (`haematite/crates/haematite/src/tree/mutate/mod.rs:102-130` `batch_mutate_owned_erased`) computes the affected window and calls `tree/mutate/window.rs:82` `rebuild_window`, which `load_entries()` the WHOLE leaf, applies the 1-event mutation, and re-persists the full leaf as a **new content-addressed node** via `tree/mutate/spine.rs:244` `.put(&Node::Leaf(leaf))` → `store/disk/node_io.rs:57` `compress_node` (zstd) → `publish_compressed_node` (`node_io.rs:28`). The old leaf blob stays on disk.
3. **Leaves are value-blind and balloon to ~73 MB.** The deployed store is **unstamped** (`aion-data/config.json` has no `format_version`), so `haematite/src/db/config.rs:280` (`derive_policy`) locks it to `TreePolicy::V1_DEFAULT` *forever*: leaf boundary fires iff `blake3(key) % 4096 == 0` (`tree/boundary.rs:26`, `DEFAULT_TARGET_SIZE = 4*1024` at `boundary.rs:1`) — an expected **4,096 entries per leaf regardless of entry size** (`tree/policy.rs:91-101`; the test `v1_default_ignores_value_length` at `policy.rs:182` documents the blindness). Transcript events average 12–17 KB, so leaves reach **73.3 MB decompressed / ~2.3 MB zstd**.
4. **So the cost of appending one ~500 B event is one full leaf blob.** Sweep leaf: 1.56 MB decompressed → ~130 KB compressed **per status line**. norn_dev leaf: 73.3 MB → ~2.3 MB compressed **per telemetry delta**. Sizes across a run form the O(n²) ladder (shard-56 top blobs: 2,303,798 → 2,303,416 → 2,302,830 → … over 646 blobs in the 2–3 MB band alone; shard-56 holds 17,195 files, 12.68 GB, median blob 817 KB, only 7,092 tiny root/internal nodes <1 KB).
5. **Nothing ever deletes superseded nodes.** Aion has **zero call sites** for haematite's vacuum/prune (grep of `crates/aion-store-haematite`, `crates/aion-server`: none; `aion-data/config.json` `sweep_interval: null` is a retired TTL-cadence key, `db/config.rs:320`, not GC). Every superseded leaf version is permanent until an offline `haem vacuum` that has never run (census §8: v1 vacuum requires the writer lock the live server holds). Reachable data per shard is the current root's tree — order of the final leaf (~2.3 MB compressed) against shard-56's 12.68 GB: **>99.8% of the hot shards is superseded-version garbage.**
6. **Cross-run amplification.** V1 leaves pack adjacent keys from MANY workflows: the shard-56 leaf holds **five workflows'** transcripts (4c4ef686 19.5 MB + 7e2192df 37.7 MB + 60ae7eeb 12.7 MB + two small); the sweep leaf holds **seven** (three sweeps + a fleet_dev + others). A live run's every event **re-persists the finished runs' full transcripts sharing its leaf**. That is why a kilobyte sweep costs 25–663 MB depending on which shard its workflow-id hashed into.

Multiplier arithmetic, per run: honest 136 KB → 73.7 MB permanent (sweep, 540×); honest ~67 MB → 6.96 GB permanent (failed norn_dev, 104×). Per single append the structural multiplier is the leaf-to-event ratio: **~977× compressed (2,359 B honest → 2,303,416 B blob), ~31,000× in serialized bytes** (fixture below).

## 3. The red-first fixture pair (for the fix lane)

Two consecutive versions of the same shard-56 leaf, written **2 seconds apart** during run `7e2192df-72f1-49da-8ae4-68cc2349ca16` (norn_dev, Failed, Aug-16 09:09–10:57 UTC):

| | blob k−1 | blob k |
|---|---|---|
| Path | `aion-data/shard-56/store/4d/f6a48078935e0777aa24a8e0200afa72de4ae41b1d3ee0770ab56b7af318b0` | `aion-data/shard-56/store/7f/9f01493155a004322d7ff429d6885e4645b77932e7a9eac9bf51e9050ee3b7` |
| mtime | 2026-08-16 09:58:28 UTC | 2026-08-16 09:58:30 UTC |
| Compressed | 2,303,798 B | 2,303,416 B |
| Decompressed | 73,301,175 B | 73,303,846 B |
| Events | 5,712 | 5,716 |

**Demonstrated superset:** every one of k−1's 5,712 `(worker_seq, store_seq)` event identities is present in k; k adds exactly 4 events, all belonging to `7e2192df` activity 1 attempt 2, emitted 09:57:06.48Z: worker_seq **56203** (Raw, 629 B), **56206** (Raw, 645 B), **56207** (Message, 409 B), **56208** (Raw, 676 B) — **2,359 honest bytes**, paid for with a new 2,303,416 B permanent blob (plus new internal/root nodes). Raw byte prefixes diverge at offset 1 (leaf header lengths shift), so the proof is by event identity, not prefix — parse both and compare `(worker_seq, store_seq)` sets. Both leaves also carry the complete transcripts of the *finished* runs `4c4ef686` (19,516,073 B) and `60ae7eeb` (12,682,960 B) — the cross-run re-persistence in one specimen.

Re-fetch: the blobs are immutable CAS files — `zstd -d -c <path>` yields the serialized leaf; events are framed JSON, delimited by `{"workflow_id":"…`, each with `worker_seq`/`store_seq`/`kind`. (Server may never be running against a copy of these paths' parent; reading the files directly is safe — they are write-once.) CLI cross-check of the live stream: `aion describe 7e2192df-72f1-49da-8ae4-68cc2349ca16` for the oplog; the transcript itself is served by the transcript read path (`read_activity_events_from`, `aion-store-haematite/src/store.rs:1628`).

## 4. Relation to aion#32 (memory retention, ~0.8 GB per sweep tick)

Same root, different symptom. #32's malloc_history stacks all terminate in **`LeafNode::deserialise`** (via `stream_index::rebuild`, `WalRecovery::recover_path`, `DiskStore::read_node`) — the *read* side of the same oversized leaves: every read/rebuild/replay must materialize a whole 1.5–73 MB leaf to touch one event, and the server retains them (~7.2 KB avg allocations = leaf entries). The 0.8 GB-per-sweep-tick memory delta and the 204 MB-per-sweep-tick disk delta are the same value-blind V1 leaves being, respectively, deserialized-and-retained and rewritten-and-retained. Fixing leaf sizing shrinks both; #32 additionally needs its unbounded re-deserialization loop found (its brief: `ablative/docs/briefs/aion-haematite-leak-brief-20260817.md`, Apollo's lane), which leaf sizing alone does not close.

The `247-transcript-spool` worktree (7 commits, worker-side disk spool + collision-safe replay dedup for transcript events across server outages) is a durability lane, not this defect: its replay dedup prevents *event-level* duplication on reconnect; it neither causes nor mitigates the leaf-rewrite amplification.

## 5. Shape of the proper fix

Haematite has already built the fix upstream: **`TreePolicy::V2` byte-weighted chunking** (on-disk format 2, `tree/policy.rs:47`, stamped via `db/config.rs` with nonzero `leaf_target_bytes`) caps leaves by bytes and isolates oversized entries. The deployed path needs: (1) aion off pinned haematite 0.8.1 onto a V2-capable release and a **format-2 migration of the unstamped `aion-data`** (unstamped = V1 forever by design — migration, not config, is the only exit); (2) **batch event appends** in `activity_publisher` (one commit per event is a second, independent multiplier); (3) a **vacuum story for superseded nodes** (aion never calls it; >99% of hot shards is reclaimable garbage) plus aion-level unpin of terminal-run transcripts; (4) at the content layer, stop persisting three full provider envelopes per turn (persist deltas; the envelope's instructions block is identical every time).

## Summary (5 lines)

1. **Mechanism:** every single activity-transcript event append rewrites its entire containing storage-tree leaf as a new permanent zstd blob — leaves hold ~4,096 entries *regardless of size* (value-blind V1 chunking, unstamped store), reaching 73 MB and packing up to 5+ workflows, so live runs re-persist finished runs' whole transcripts per event, and no vacuum ever deletes the superseded versions.
2. **Multiplier:** honest content → permanent store = 540× for a sweep tick (136 KB → 73.7 MB), ~104–112× for norn_dev runs (67 MB → 6.96 GB failed; 26.6 MB → 2.98 GB completed); per-append the fixture shows 2,359 honest bytes buying a 2,303,416-byte permanent blob (~977×).
3. **File:line:** `aion-server/src/activity_publisher.rs:183` + `aion-store-haematite/src/store.rs:1617` (append-of-one per event) → haematite `tree/mutate/window.rs:82` `rebuild_window` + `tree/mutate/spine.rs:244` `.put(&Node::Leaf)` (whole-leaf rewrite) under `tree/boundary.rs:1,26` / `db/config.rs:280` (value-blind V1 policy, locked in by the unstamped `aion-data/config.json`).
4. **#32 same root:** yes — its leak stacks end in `LeafNode::deserialise` of these same oversized leaves (read-side materialization + retention), though #32's unbounded re-deserialization loop is an additional defect leaf-sizing alone won't close.
5. **Proper fix:** migrate `aion-data` to haematite format-2 byte-weighted chunking (already implemented upstream: `TreePolicy::V2`), batch event appends per commit, add a vacuum/unpin path for superseded nodes, and stop persisting three full provider envelopes per LLM turn.

---

1	//! The §3.4 translation point — the single place Norn's native event/command shapes are named.
2	//!
3	//! Two directions, both pure and independently testable:
4	//!
5	//! - **OUT:** [`notification_to_event`] maps a Norn `event/*` JSON-RPC notification (its `method`
6	//!   and `params`, as emitted by Norn's `agent_event_to_value` with `agent_id`/`agent_role` added)
7	//!   into a neutral [`ActivityEvent`]. Anything the adapter cannot classify falls through to
8	//!   [`ActivityEventKind::Raw`], so nothing is ever silently dropped.
9	//! - **IN:** [`intervention_to_request`] maps a neutral [`InterventionKind`] into the Norn
10	//!   `intervene/*` request (method + params). A primitive Norn does not advertise
11	//!   ([`InterventionKind::PauseResume`] / [`UpdateBudget`] / [`RespondToApproval`]) is rejected
12	//!   with [`HarnessError::CapabilityNotSupported`] and never sent.
13	//!
14	//! Plus [`parse_capabilities`], which gates the `initialize` result on the driven-mode protocol
15	//! version (`norn-driven/1`) and reads it into the neutral [`InterventionCapabilities`] the
16	//! server/console gate on, and [`run_result_to_outcome`], which interprets the `run/execute`
17	//! versioned stop envelope into the canonical [`AgentOutcome`] record (or the honest error a
18	//! non-completed stop — or an output the agent-outcome contract cannot carry — is).
19	//!
20	//! [`UpdateBudget`]: InterventionKind::UpdateBudget
21	//! [`RespondToApproval`]: InterventionKind::RespondToApproval
22	
23	use aion_core::{
24	    ActivityEvent, ActivityEventKind, InterventionCapabilities, InterventionKind,
25	    InterventionPrimitive, MessageRole, ProgressDetail, StopKind,
26	};
27	use aion_integrations::HarnessError;
28	use chrono::Utc;
29	use serde_json::{Value, json};
30	use uuid::Uuid;

34	/// Identity carried on every event a session produces, stamped from the run spec + handshake.
35	///
36	/// The `(workflow, run, activity, attempt)` key and the per-notification `agent_id`/`agent_role`
37	/// (read from the notification params) together fill an [`ActivityEvent`]'s identity fields; the
38	/// producer-side ordering fields are filled by the session (a best-effort local sequence).
39	#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
40	pub struct EventIdentity {
41	    /// The workflow this run belongs to.
42	    pub workflow_id: aion_core::WorkflowId,
43	    /// The concrete run of that workflow this attempt belongs to — stamped from the run spec,
44	    /// never synthesised here. It is the axis that keeps two generations of a continue-as-new
45	    /// chain from writing one fused transcript.
46	    pub run_id: aion_core::RunId,
47	    /// The activity within the workflow.
48	    pub activity_id: aion_core::ActivityId,
49	    /// The attempt number of the run.
50	    pub attempt: u32,
51	}

53	/// Reads Norn's `initialize` result into the neutral [`InterventionCapabilities`], gating on the
54	/// driven-mode protocol version first.
55	///
56	/// The result must advertise `protocol: "norn-driven/1"` (which replaced the old
57	/// `protocolVersion: "2.0"`); a missing or different value is a [`HarnessError::Protocol`] naming
58	/// the expected and received values — the honest "your norn binary is stale" signal, surfaced
59	/// before any run is issued.
60	///
61	/// Norn advertises a `capabilities.interventions` array of neutral primitive labels
62	/// (`inject_message`, `cancel`, …). Unknown labels are ignored (forward-compat), and a missing
63	/// array yields the empty (observability-only) set — never an error, because an empty capability
64	/// advertisement is first-class.
65	///
66	/// # Errors
67	///
68	/// Returns [`HarnessError::Protocol`] when the `protocol` field is missing or is not exactly
69	/// [`protocol::PROTOCOL_VERSION`]; a present-but-wrong value (any JSON type) is rendered
70	/// verbatim in the message.
71	pub fn parse_capabilities(
72	    initialize_result: &Value,
73	) -> Result<InterventionCapabilities, HarnessError> {
74	    match initialize_result.get(protocol::PROTOCOL_KEY) {
75	        Some(received) if received.as_str() == Some(protocol::PROTOCOL_VERSION) => {}
76	        // A present-but-wrong value — including a non-string — is reported as the JSON actually
77	        // received (a string renders quoted), never misdescribed as a missing field.
78	        Some(received) => {
79	            return Err(HarnessError::protocol(format!(
80	                "norn driven-mode protocol mismatch: expected {:?}, received {received} — \
81	                 the norn binary is stale or incompatible with this adapter",
82	                protocol::PROTOCOL_VERSION,
83	            )));
84	        }
85	        None => {
86	            return Err(HarnessError::protocol(format!(
87	                "norn driven-mode protocol mismatch: expected {:?}, received no `{}` field — \
88	                 the norn binary is stale or incompatible with this adapter",
89	                protocol::PROTOCOL_VERSION,
90	                protocol::PROTOCOL_KEY,
91	            )));
92	        }
93	    }
94	    let labels = initialize_result
95	        .get(protocol::CAPABILITIES_KEY)
96	        .and_then(|caps| caps.get(protocol::INTERVENTIONS_KEY))
97	        .and_then(Value::as_array);
98	    let Some(labels) = labels else {
99	        return Ok(InterventionCapabilities::none());
100	    };
101	    let primitives = labels
102	        .iter()
103	        .filter_map(Value::as_str)
104	        .filter_map(capability_label_to_primitive);
105	    Ok(InterventionCapabilities::from_primitives(primitives))
106	}

111	/// Maps a neutral capability label Norn advertises onto its [`InterventionPrimitive`].
112	///
113	/// Returns `None` for a label this neutral set does not enumerate, so an unknown label is ignored
114	/// rather than fabricated into a primitive.
115	fn capability_label_to_primitive(label: &str) -> Option<InterventionPrimitive> {
116	    match label {
117	        protocol::CAPABILITY_INJECT_MESSAGE => Some(InterventionPrimitive::InjectMessage),
118	        protocol::CAPABILITY_CANCEL => Some(InterventionPrimitive::Cancel),
119	        protocol::CAPABILITY_PAUSE_RESUME => Some(InterventionPrimitive::PauseResume),
120	        protocol::CAPABILITY_UPDATE_BUDGET => Some(InterventionPrimitive::UpdateBudget),
121	        protocol::CAPABILITY_RESPOND_TO_APPROVAL => Some(InterventionPrimitive::RespondToApproval),
122	        _ => None,
123	    }

126	/// The Norn `intervene/*` request a neutral command maps onto: a method plus its params.
127	///
128	/// Only the two primitives Norn advertises produce a request; the other three are rejected before
129	/// this returns, so a request is never built for an unsupported primitive.
130	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
131	pub struct NornRequest {
132	    /// The Norn `intervene/*` method name.
133	    pub method: &'static str,
134	    /// The request params.
135	    pub params: Value,
136	}

138	/// Maps a neutral [`InterventionKind`] into the Norn `intervene/*` request that carries it.
139	///
140	/// `InjectMessage` → `intervene/injectMessage` (with a `text` + neutral `priority`), `Cancel` →
141	/// `intervene/cancel` (with a `reason`). The three primitives Norn does not advertise
142	/// (`PauseResume`, `UpdateBudget`, `RespondToApproval`) are rejected with
143	/// [`HarnessError::CapabilityNotSupported`] and NEVER sent — the adapter does not fabricate a
144	/// Norn mechanism that does not exist.
145	///
146	/// # Errors
147	///
148	/// Returns [`HarnessError::CapabilityNotSupported`] for a primitive Norn does not support.
149	pub fn intervention_to_request(kind: &InterventionKind) -> Result<NornRequest, HarnessError> {
150	    match kind {
151	        InterventionKind::InjectMessage { text, priority } => {
152	            let priority_label = match priority {
153	                aion_core::InjectPriority::Interrupt => protocol::PRIORITY_INTERRUPT,
154	                aion_core::InjectPriority::Normal => protocol::PRIORITY_NORMAL,
155	            };
156	            Ok(NornRequest {
157	                method: protocol::METHOD_INTERVENE_INJECT,
158	                params: json!({
159	                    protocol::PARAM_TEXT: text,
160	                    protocol::PARAM_PRIORITY: priority_label,
161	                }),
162	            })
163	        }
164	        InterventionKind::Cancel { reason } => Ok(NornRequest {
165	            method: protocol::METHOD_INTERVENE_CANCEL,
166	            params: json!({ protocol::PARAM_REASON: reason }),
167	        }),
168	        InterventionKind::PauseResume { .. }
169	        | InterventionKind::UpdateBudget { .. }
170	        | InterventionKind::RespondToApproval { .. } => Err(
171	            HarnessError::capability_not_supported(primitive_label(kind.primitive())),
172	        ),
173	    }
174	}
175	
176	/// A neutral, human-readable label for a primitive (used in the capability-gate rejection).
177	fn primitive_label(primitive: InterventionPrimitive) -> &'static str {
178	    match primitive {
179	        InterventionPrimitive::InjectMessage => protocol::CAPABILITY_INJECT_MESSAGE,
180	        InterventionPrimitive::Cancel => protocol::CAPABILITY_CANCEL,
181	        InterventionPrimitive::PauseResume => protocol::CAPABILITY_PAUSE_RESUME,
182	        InterventionPrimitive::UpdateBudget => protocol::CAPABILITY_UPDATE_BUDGET,
183	        InterventionPrimitive::RespondToApproval => protocol::CAPABILITY_RESPOND_TO_APPROVAL,
184	    }
185	}

1	//! Durable transcript read API (lane #229): the REST twin of the events pair.
2	//!
3	//! `POST /workflows/transcript` fetches the retained transcript of one
4	//! `(workflow, run, activity, attempt)` stream from the durable `O` keyspace,
5	//! and `POST /workflows/transcripts` enumerates one RUN's retained streams.
6	//!
7	//! Together they mirror the workflow-history pair: `/workflows/describe` is the
8	//! socket-free history read, the `/events/stream` subscription is the live
9	//! tail — and for transcripts this pair is the socket-free read while the
10	//! `/events/stream` transcript subscription remains the live-tail attach. A
11	//! client that wants both does a REST fetch first, then attaches the WS with
12	//! `after_seq` = the last fetched `store_seq` (the publisher's subscribe path
13	//! dedups the splice seam on `store_seq`).
14	//!
15	//! Both endpoints are namespace-scoped through the SAME per-workflow gate the
16	//! transcript WS subscription uses ([`gate_transcript_workflow`]), so a caller
17	//! probing a foreign or nonexistent workflow receives the guard's anti-leak
18	//! `not_found`, never a transcript. An authorized workflow with nothing
19	//! retained answers `200` with an empty list — the honest answer for an old
20	//! run recorded before retention existed, never an error.
21	//!
22	//! # The run axis is required on both requests
23	//!
24	//! A continue-as-new chain reuses one workflow id while activity ordinals and
25	//! attempt numbers restart in every generation, so a request naming only
26	//! `(workflow, activity, attempt)` does not identify a stream. `run_id` is
27	//! required rather than optional-with-a-latest-run-default, because a default
28	//! would answer a question the caller did not ask, and would do it silently.
29	
30	use aion_core::{ActivityEvent, ActivityId, RunId, WorkflowId};
31	use aion_proto::WireError;
32	use aion_store::{ActivityRecord, ActivityStreamKey};
33	use axum::{Json, extract::State};
34	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
35	
36	use super::auth::HttpCaller;
37	use super::error::HttpWireError;
38	use crate::ServerState;
39	use crate::config::MAX_TRANSCRIPT_WINDOW_LIMIT;
40	use crate::stream::gate_transcript_workflow;
41	
42	/// The transcript-fetch request body: the target stream's full identity plus
43	/// the namespace the workflow runs under (the auth scope), an optional resume
44	/// cursor, and optional bounded-window selectors.
45	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
46	pub(crate) struct TranscriptFetchRequest {
47	    /// The namespace the target workflow runs under (the auth scope).
48	    pub namespace: String,
49	    /// The target workflow.
50	    pub workflow_id: WorkflowId,
51	    /// The target run of that workflow — the second stream axis. REQUIRED: two
52	    /// generations of one continue-as-new chain share every other coordinate.
53	    pub run_id: RunId,
54	    /// The target activity within the workflow.
55	    pub activity_id: ActivityId,
56	    /// The target attempt — the fourth stream axis.
57	    pub attempt: u32,
58	    /// Read records with `store_seq >= from_seq`; omitted reads the whole
59	    /// retained transcript from `store_seq == 0`.
60	    #[serde(default)]
61	    pub from_seq: Option<u64>,
62	    /// Maximum records to return. Omitted preserves the unbounded legacy read.
63	    #[serde(default)]
64	    pub limit: Option<u32>,
65	    /// Return only the last `n` retained records. Mutually exclusive with
66	    /// `from_seq`.
67	    #[serde(default)]
68	    pub last: Option<u32>,
69	}
70	
71	/// The transcript-fetch response body: the retained events, in `store_seq`
72	/// order, each carrying its `store_seq`. Empty for a stream with nothing
73	/// retained (an unknown or pre-retention run).
74	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
75	pub(crate) struct TranscriptFetchResponse {
76	    /// The retained transcript events in `store_seq` order.
77	    pub events: Vec<ActivityEvent>,
78	    /// First omitted `store_seq` when `limit` truncated the response.
79	    pub next_from_seq: Option<u64>,
80	    /// Stream head at read time: the next durable `store_seq`.
81	    pub head_seq: u64,
82	}
83	
84	/// The stream-enumeration request body: the workflow whose retained transcript
85	/// streams to list, plus the namespace it runs under (the auth scope).
86	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
87	pub(crate) struct TranscriptStreamsRequest {
88	    /// The namespace the target workflow runs under (the auth scope).
89	    pub namespace: String,
90	    /// The workflow whose retained transcript streams to enumerate.
91	    pub workflow_id: WorkflowId,
92	    /// The run of that workflow whose retained streams to enumerate. REQUIRED:
93	    /// enumerating a whole continue-as-new chain would return several
94	    /// generations' streams under pairwise-colliding coordinates.
95	    pub run_id: RunId,
96	}
97	
98	/// One retained transcript stream of the workflow run.
99	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
100	pub(crate) struct TranscriptStreamEntry {
101	    /// The run the stream belongs to. Echoed on every row so a row lifted out of
102	    /// the response still names its generation.
103	    pub run_id: RunId,
104	    /// The activity within the workflow.
105	    pub activity_id: ActivityId,
106	    /// The attempt number — the fourth stream axis.
107	    pub attempt: u32,
108	    /// Next `store_seq` to be written == count of retained records.
109	    pub head: u64,
110	}
111	
112	/// The stream-enumeration response body: every retained stream, ordered by
113	/// `(activity, attempt)`. Empty for a workflow with no retained transcript.
114	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
115	pub(crate) struct TranscriptStreamsResponse {
116	    /// The RUN's retained transcript streams.
117	    pub streams: Vec<TranscriptStreamEntry>,
118	}
119	
120	/// `POST /workflows/transcript`.
121	///
122	/// Namespace-gates the caller (byte-identical to the transcript WS
123	/// subscription), then reads the retained `O` tail of the addressed stream
124	/// from `from_seq` (default `0`). An unknown or pre-retention stream returns
125	/// `200` with empty `events`, a null `next_from_seq`, and `head_seq == 0` — the
126	/// honest answer, never an error; only an authorization failure or a store fault
127	/// is an HTTP error.
128	pub(crate) async fn fetch_transcript(
129	    State(state): State<ServerState>,
130	    HttpCaller(caller): HttpCaller,
131	    Json(request): Json<TranscriptFetchRequest>,
132	) -> Result<Json<TranscriptFetchResponse>, HttpWireError> {
133	    gate_transcript_workflow(&state, &caller, &request.namespace, &request.workflow_id)
134	        .await
135	        .map_err(|error| HttpWireError(error.to_wire_error()))?;
136	    if request.from_seq.is_some() && request.last.is_some() {
137	        return Err(HttpWireError(WireError::invalid_input(
138	            "transcript from_seq and last are mutually exclusive",
139	        )));
140	    }
141	    let key = ActivityStreamKey::new(
142	        request.workflow_id,
143	        request.run_id,
144	        request.activity_id,
145	        request.attempt,
146	    );
147	    let from_seq = request.from_seq.map_or(0, |seq| seq);
148	    let read_from = request.last.map_or(from_seq, |_last| 0);
149	    let ranged = state
150	        .transcript_publisher()
151	        .replay_from(&key, read_from)
152	        .await
153	        .map_err(|error| HttpWireError(crate::ServerError::from(error).to_wire_error()))?;
154	    let mut records = if ranged.is_empty() && read_from != 0 {
155	        state
156	            .transcript_publisher()
157	            .replay_from(&key, 0)
158	            .await
159	            .map_err(|error| HttpWireError(crate::ServerError::from(error).to_wire_error()))?
160	    } else {
161	        ranged
162	    };
163	    let head_seq = transcript_head(&records)?;
164	    if request.last.is_none() && read_from != 0 {
165	        records.retain(|record| record.store_seq >= read_from);
166	    }

171	            )))
